record.context_brief: Ample versus virtually ample versus weakly ample
record.original_question: What is the precise relationship among ample fields, virtually ample fields, and weakly ample fields? In particular, if a field K is called virtually ample when some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample when every K-curve C becomes infinite over some finite extension L/K, must every weakly ample field be virtually ample, and must every virtually ample field already be ample?

evidence.quote: A field K is virtually ample if some finite extension of K is ample. Exchanging quantifiers in this definition we get a weaker condition: A field K is called weakly ample if for every K-curve C there exists a finite extension L of K such that C(L) is infinite.
Question IV. What is the relation between ample, virtually ample, and weakly ample fields? Is every weakly ample field virtually ample? Is every virtually ample field ample?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A field $K$ is called ample (also: large) if for every smooth, geometrically integral $K$-variety $V$ with $V(K)\neq\emptyset$, the set $V(K)$ is Zariski dense in $V$ (equivalently, every smooth $K$-curve with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points). A field $K$ is called virtually ample if there exists a finite field extension $L/K$ such that $L$ is ample. A field $K$ is called weakly ample if for every smooth geometrically integral $K$-curve $C$ there exists a finite field extension $L/K$ (depending on $C$) such that $C(L)$ is infinite.

Problem. Determine the precise logical relationships among the three classes "ample", "virtually ample", and "weakly ample" of fields. In particular, settle the following two implications:

(a) Does every weakly ample field have to be virtually ample?

(b) Does every virtually ample field have to be ample?

That is, are the three classes the same, or are the inclusions ample $\subseteq$ virtually ample $\subseteq$ weakly ample strict?
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) has been resolved negatively: P. Srinivasan (Israel J. Math., 2019; arXiv:1810.05184) constructed a virtually ample field that is not ample, so the inclusion ample ⊊ virtually ample is strict. The question of whether every weakly ample field is virtually ample (part (a)) does not appear to have been settled in the literature located, so the full relationship among the three classes remains only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: A virtually ample field that is not ample
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a field L of characteristic zero with a quadratic extension M such that M is ample but L is not ample.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a virtually ample field that is not ample, settling part (b) negatively.

status_evidence.title: A virtually ample field that is not ample (Israel J. Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version showing strict inclusion of ample fields inside virtually ample fields.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms that virtually ample does not imply ample.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in the Theory of Ample Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems concerning ample fields, including questions about virtually ample and weakly ample fields.
status_evidence.claim: Records the relations among ample, virtually ample, and weakly ample as a stated open problem.
